title: Financial Services Configuration Consistency
business: A regional banking firm managing microservices across multiple Kubernetes clusters.
problem: Manual kubectl interventions by developers caused configuration drift, leading to inconsistent security policies and failed deployments in production environments.
solution: Argo CD implements a GitOps controller that continuously reconciles the live cluster state against a version-controlled Git repository, automatically detecting and alerting on deviations.
steps: Define the target application state using Helm charts or Kustomize manifests stored in a centralized Git repository.
Register the target Kubernetes clusters with the Argo CD controller.
Create an Application resource in Argo CD that points to the Git repository path and the target cluster namespace.
Enable automated synchronization to ensure the controller overwrites manual changes with the Git-defined desired state.
Monitor the Argo CD dashboard for OutOfSync status indicators to identify unauthorized configuration changes.
outcome: The organization achieves a single source of truth where all cluster modifications are auditable, versioned, and automatically enforced, eliminating manual configuration errors.
limitation: Argo CD does not prevent users with cluster-admin privileges from making out-of-band changes; it only detects and potentially reverts them. Verification requires checking the Application status in the UI or CLI for an OutOfSync state.

questions.question: In Financial Services Configuration Consistency, what is the primary mechanism used to address configuration drift?
options: Manual reconciliation by developers using kubectl
Automated controller monitoring of live state against Git
External audit logs generated by the cloud provider
questions.explanation: The solution relies on the Argo CD controller comparing the live state to the Git source of truth to identify and fix drift.
questions.evidence: Argo CD implements a GitOps controller that continuously reconciles the live cluster state against a version-controlled Git repository, automatically detecting and alerting on deviations.

questions.question: In Financial Services Configuration Consistency, what is a known limitation regarding cluster modifications?
options: Argo CD prevents all unauthorized access to the cluster
Argo CD cannot detect drift if the Git repository is empty
Users with high privileges can still make manual changes that the controller must then revert
The controller requires manual intervention for every sync operation
questions.explanation: Argo CD acts as a reconciler; it does not block the API server from accepting changes, but rather detects them after the fact.
questions.evidence: Argo CD does not prevent users with cluster-admin privileges from making out-of-band changes; it only detects and potentially reverts them.
